newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt airport back to normal after evacuation.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt airport back to normal after evacuation.

text.p: Service at Frankfurt international airport returned to normal on Monday after firefighters evacuated hundreds of people from one terminal building late Sunday, following a smoke alarm.
"Services are back to normal," Wolfgang Schwalm, a spokesman at the airport, continental Europe's busiest, told German radio.
One woman was slightly injured when firefighters shut down Hall B in the airport's Terminal One after smoke was spotted coming out of an air-conditioning system.
Schwalm said the smoke was likely to have been caused by a burning cigarette, which may have been carelessly discarded. He stressed that there was never any open fire.
The incident occurred almost exactly one year after a fire tore through Duesseldorf airport, Germany's second largest, killing 17 people and injuring hundreds.

Schwalm warned against finding similarities between last year's deadly inferno and the Frankfurt incident. "The head of the fire brigade said that there were no parallels in this case with the Duesseldorf fire," Schwalm said.
Experts charged with investigating the Duesseldorf fire however warned that what happened in Duesseldorf could happen again at another German airport.

"A similar catastrophe could occur at any time at another German airport or in another public building," the German news magazine Der Spiegel quoted an unnamed member of the expert commission has saying.

This expert said many fire precautions were not implemented, but Schwalm denied this was the case in Frankfurt. "We read the report from the Duesseldorf fire and we implemented the changes," Schwalm said.

The closure of the terminal building caused chaos in the early evening as flights were redirected to other terminals and confused passengers sought to track down their luggage. There were some delays in flights.
"It was very lucky that this happened at this hour," airport spokesman Wolf-Dieter Schaller said, adding that there were usually many more passengers in that building during the day.
